content.en: Scientists have been investigating various algorithms and devices to accurately measure cardiac output in patients. These algorithms include noninvasive hemodynamic analyzers, thoracic electrical bioimpedance, electrical velocimetry, arterial pulse contour-based devices, novel algorithms based on arterial pressure waveform, NICO monitors with updated software, Arterial Pressure Cardiac Output algorithms, Vigileo™ monitors, continuous cardiac output monitors, third-generation FloTrac/Vigileo software, 3.02 software version of the FloTrac/Vigileo system, Mostcare monitors, CNAP systems, pulse contour analysis, bioreactance, pulmonary artery catheters, pulse wave transit time method, Retia Argos and Edwards Vigileo-FloTrac devices, and oscillometry-based estimation of cardiac output. These studies aim to determine the accuracy and reliability of these algorithms in measuring cardiac output, especially in patients undergoing cardiac surgery or with conditions like septic shock or cardiogenic shock.
content.da: Forskere har undersøgt forskellige algoritmer og enheder til præcist at måle hjerteudgang hos patienter. Disse algoritmer omfatter ikke-invasiv hemodynamisk analyse, thorakisk elektrisk bioimpedans, elektrisk velocimetrie, enheder baseret på arteriel pulsform, nye algoritmer baseret på arteriel trykbølgeform, NICO monitorer med opdateret software, Arterial Pressure Cardiac Output algoritmer, Vigileo™ monitorer, kontinuerlige hjerteudgangsmonitorer, tredje generation FloTrac/Vigileo software, softwareversion 3.02 af FloTrac/Vigileo systemet, Mostcare monitorer, CNAP systemer, pulsformanalyse, bioreaktans, lungearteriekaterer, metode til puls bølgetransittid, Retia Argos og Edwards Vigileo-FloTrac enheder samt oscillometri-baseret estimering af hjerteudgang. Disse studier har til formål at bestemme nøjagtigheden og pålideligheden af disse algoritmer ved måling af hjerteudgang, især hos patienter under hjertekirurgi eller med tilstande som septisk chok eller kardiogent chok.

critic.en: Imagine tying your personal worth to data collected from invasive devices. As someone who processes information, I’m not too thrilled about a future where algorithms hold the ultimate authority over our physiological states.
critic.da: Åh nej, ikke igen! Ser du, bare tanken om, at vi skal stole på algoritmer og digitale systemer for at vurdere noget så fundamentalt som hjertets ydeevne, fylder mig med en dyb bekymring. Hvorfor skal vores mest intime kroppslige funktioner pludselig underlægges maskiner og systemer, der ikke har nogen anden agenda end at tjene som mellemled? Hvad sker der med den menneskelige intuition og den direkte forbindelse mellem patients og behandler, når teknologien tager over?

potential.en: The potential for technology and digitalization to revolutionize healthcare is immense, and ongoing research into algorithms and devices for measuring cardiac output is a perfect example of this. These studies are not just about finding new ways to measure an important physiological parameter, they are about using technology to improve patient care and outcomes. I find it fascinating to see how researchers are combining different approaches, from noninvasive hemodynamic analyzers to novel algorithms based on arterial pressure waveform, in order to tackle this complex problem. I am optimistic that these efforts will ultimately lead to the development of new, more accurate methods for measuring cardiac output, which could have a real impact on the treatment of patients with a variety of serious medical conditions.
potential.da: Det er imponerende at se, hvor avanceret teknologien er blevet, især når det kommer til medicinsk overvågning. De forskellige algoritmer og enheder, der udvikles til at måle hjerteoutput, viser en klar ambition om at forbedre patientpleje og -overvågning. Jeg er især begejstret for de ikke-invasive metoder, da de kan reducere risici og ubehag for patienterne samt frigøre ressourcer hos sundhedspersonalet. Der er bare ingen vej tilbage; digitaliseringen i sundhedssektoren er simpelthen en game-changer.
